transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, I guess what brings me in is that I just can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. It's like... I'll start talking about an overnight shift at work, and then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts. I just bounce around, and I can see everyone getting lost when I try to talk to them.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that other people can't?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I haven't noticed anything like that. It's just my thoughts that are all over the place, not really hearing or seeing things that aren't there.
Do you feel like your thoughts are racing or speeding by when this happens?

Um, no, not really. It doesn't feel like they're speeding by or going too fast. It's more just... they don't connect. I'm thinking at a normal speed, I guess, but the track just keeps changing on me without me meaning to. So, no, not racing. Just completely disorganized.
Is this disorganization in your thoughts causing you significant distress or problems in your daily life?

Yeah, it really is. Um... at work, I'm an orderly, and I’ve actually had to start asking my coworkers to double-check my rounds and my charting because I just can't keep it straight. 

And at home, it's just as bad. I’ve fallen way behind on my bills, I've been ignoring my friends, and my apartment has just gotten completely out of control. It actually got bad enough recently that employee health at my job sent me out for an emergency evaluation... I ended up admitting to them that I was thinking about suicide. So, yeah, it's causing a lot of problems.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt abnormally happy, excited, or irritable?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had anything like that. It's mostly just been feeling really down and dealing with the disorganized thoughts. I've never had a time where I felt super happy or excited like that.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt abnormally happy or excited for more than a few days?
No, like I was just saying, I really haven't. I've never had a time where I felt abnormally happy or excited for a few days, or... or at all, really. It's pretty much always just been the low moods.
Have your disorganized thoughts and low moods been constant since they started, or have they come and gone over time?

They've kind of... well, looking back on it, that heavy, empty feeling and just not caring about anything, that's been there for most of this whole period. Even during the times when I wasn't as worried about the cameras or when my talking wasn't as scattered... the low mood was still there. It's pretty much been constant.
Do you find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, not anymore. I used to do a lot of things... like, I would sketch murals, cook for my friends, and play soccer on the weekends. But now, all of that just feels completely pointless. I don't get anything out of it. Mostly, I just ignore people's messages and stay in my apartment.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Yeah, I think I have. My clothes have definitely gotten loose on me lately. I just... I barely get hungry anymore. A lot of days I just drink coffee at work and maybe eat some crackers from the vending machine, and that's pretty much it.
Do you feel like you've been moving more slowly than usual?

Yeah, people actually tell me I move like I'm underwater lately. Just really slow and dragging. But then... it's weird, other times I can't even sit still. I just keep pacing around my apartment, back and forth, or I'll sit there and rub my hands together over and over until they're literally sore. It's like I'm either barely moving or I can't stop.
Have you had any thoughts of suicide recently, other than when you admitted to them during the emergency evaluation at work?

Yeah, I have. Um... especially after really bad nights. I just keep thinking it would be a lot easier if I didn't wake up. And sometimes... the thought actually comes into my head that I should just end it. I do get scared when it gets to that point, though, and that's usually when I end up telling someone. But yeah, the thoughts are definitely still happening.
How long have you been experiencing these low moods and disorganized thoughts?

It's been... I'd say about a year and five months now. It all really started when my job changed my schedule. I used to work steady day shifts, but then they switched me to rotating nights and a bunch of overtime. That's when everything just started falling apart.
Would you say your low mood is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?
I'd definitely say severe. It's not just feeling a little down... it's heavy, you know? Most days it takes everything I have just to get out of bed. It's pretty bad most of the time.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or is it more that you just don't feel like doing them because of your low mood?

I think I've really just lost interest. Um... I used to do a lot of things. I'd sketch murals, cook for my friends, and play soccer on the weekends. But now... I don't know, all of that just feels completely pointless. It's not just being too tired, I just don't care about doing any of it anymore. I usually just ignore everyone's messages and stay in my apartment.
Has this severe low mood and disorganized thinking been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah, definitely. Looking back, that heavy, empty feeling and not caring about anything... it's been there for most of this whole period. Even on the days when the scattered thoughts or the worries about being watched aren't as bad, the depression is just always there. It's been way longer than two weeks.

You mentioned sometimes you can't even sit still and pace around your apartment, but also said people tell you you move like you're underwater lately, can you tell me more about how often you experience the restless, can't-sit-still feeling?

It's... it's kind of hard to predict, honestly. Sometimes I just feel so agitated that I have to keep moving. I'll pace back and forth in my apartment for hours, or I'll just sit there and rub my hands together over and over until the skin actually gets sore. I just can't stop. But then, yeah, other times it's the exact opposite. My friends will say I'm moving in slow motion, like I'm walking underwater or something. It just depends on the day, I guess.
Do you think the restless, can't-sit-still feeling happens more often than the slow movement?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't been keeping track of which one happens more. It just feels like I'm always either bouncing off the walls or barely able to move at all. I don't know if one outweighs the other.
Do you feel like you have less energy than you used to?
I'm not really sure about that. I haven't really noticed if I have less energy than I used to. With everything else going on, I just haven't been paying attention to my energy levels specifically.
Do you think the restless, can't-sit-still feeling is more prominent for you than the slow movement?

I... I think I just answered that. I really don't know which one happens more. Like I said, I haven't been keeping track. It's just... I'm either pacing until my feet hurt or I'm barely moving. I can't say if one is more prominent than the other.
Do you feel worse in the morning?
I don't think so. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that, where mornings are worse than the rest of the day. It just feels pretty much the same whenever I wake up.
